decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm elbow-up approach to the yellow cup, lifting before moving inward; left arm stays at origin.
Advance above the cup while pitching the right gripper downward, preserving the established elbow-up branch.
Align the open right gripper above the cup's right rim; fingers will enter from above rather than push the cup sideways.
Lower the open fingers toward the cup rim, keeping the cup upright and checking depth before closing.
Pinch the cup's right rim and begin a small vertical retention test; keep the cup orientation unchanged.
Lift the rim-held cup vertically to verify retention. Start the left arm toward the vase, with both arms remaining on their own sides.
Cup appears retained above the table. Bring the open left fingers toward the vase neck for an upright repositioning grasp.
Advance around the vase neck and close the left gripper, keeping the held cup stationary and closed.
Test the vase-neck grasp with a small straight lift; watch for the vase moving with the left fingers.
The vase did not visibly follow the lift. Reopen, reach slightly farther and lower around the neck, then reclose; cup remains held.
Allow the neck grasp to settle at the observed pose, then test retention with a gentle 2 cm lift without further downward pressure.
The fingers still close above the vase neck. Retract and lower the open left gripper for a true side grasp below the lip, avoiding pressure on the rim.
Align the left finger pair around the visible lower neck, advance slightly, close, and test with a small lift. Keep the cup fixed.
Lift the neck-grasped vase clear of the table and begin moving it inward; verify that it follows the left hand before the longer transfer.
Vase retention is still unconfirmed. Reopen and align lower and farther around the cylindrical neck rather than the lip before another grasp.
The side approach is contacting the lip without secure retention. Lift away and transition the left hand to a top-down rim pinch, keeping the cup stationary.
Replan from the unchanged observed pose after the IK rejection, starting with a very small lift to clear contact and preserve continuity.
Continue lifting and pitching the open left fingers downward above the vase, staying well left of the held cup.
Align the left gripper for a top-down neck grasp, compensating the fingertip shift as the wrist pitches downward.
Center the neck deeper between the open downward fingers, then start closing gently around its outside.
Close around the now-centered vase neck and test a short vertical lift; keep the right-hand cup still and closed.
Check the top-down neck grasp by lifting and translating slightly inward; only proceed with repositioning if the vase follows.
Leave the unmoving vase in place. Clear the left hand and bring the retained cup toward the center for a left-hand transfer, without crossing arms.
Present the cup slightly toward center and rotate the left gripper for an opposite-side body grasp; retain all balls with only a modest cup tilt.
Approach the cup body with the left fingers from the left side while the right hand maintains the rim grasp.
Bring the left open fingers around the cup body for handover, stopping short of the right wrist and keeping each EE on its own side.
Lower the left grasp below the right rim-holding fingers to avoid hand contact, then approach the cup's lower body slowly.
Close the left fingers around the cup body, then progressively release the right rim grip while both wrists remain stationary.
Carefully withdraw the open right fingers and test whether the cup follows the closed left hand; avoid tilting further until retention is visible.
The cup is upright on the table with the balls still inside. Reopen the left hand and approach from the left with a shallower finger angle for a direct body grasp.
Lower the left fingers around the upright cup body and start closing only after the fingers straddle its sides.
Finish the left-hand body grasp slightly below the cup rim, then lift only a little to verify it moves with the fingers.
The fingers closed above the cup rather than retaining it. Reopen and lower farther to contact the cup sides below its rim.
Test the lower left-hand grasp with a slow vertical lift, watching the cup's motion relative to the fingers.
The cup now follows the left hand. Lift and carry it left toward the vase without changing its tilt, keeping the grip closed.
The cup slipped onto its side but balls remain visible inside. Reorient the left open gripper above the sideways cup for a transverse body grasp.
Capture the sideways cup across its body and stop further rolling; some balls are now outside, so transfer is incomplete.
Lift the captured cup and turn its mouth upward, compensating the fingertip arc with leftward wrist motion to avoid sweeping the loose balls.
The previous grip missed the cup. Recenter the downward left fingers over its middle, correcting the lateral offset before lowering again.
Lower the open fingers past the cup's upper surface, close across its sides, and make a small lift to assess retention before further rotation.
Test the cup grasp with a straight 5 cm lift, keeping the fingers closed and orientation fixed; spilled balls still require recovery.
The cup is now retained. Turn it upright while preparing the right gripper to recover the spilled balls from above.
Finish uprighting the retained cup as a receptacle. Lower the open right gripper toward the nearest loose ball, checking alignment before closing.
Use smaller left-wrist increments after the continuity rejection. Align the right fingers over the nearest loose ball while descending slowly.
Bring the right fingertips down to the nearest ball and begin a gentle pinch; keep the cup stationary while assessing alignment.
Correct the right fingertip alignment toward the nearer ball, lower slightly, and close before a minimal lift test.
Refine the right pinch around the ball visible beside the closed fingers, then lift a few millimeters to verify retention rather than sweeping it.
Lift before re-centering over the isolated ball to avoid rolling it; descend with the ball between the right fingertips and close.
Lift the right pinch to check for a retained ball while gradually uprighting the empty cup; use small left wrist increments near the continuity limit.
No ball is visibly retained. Re-center the open right fingers over the isolated front ball before descending; continue slowly uprighting the cup.
The isolated ball is centered between the open right fingers. Lower to its sides, close without lateral motion, then make a short retention test.
The ball remains on the table just beyond the pinching zone. Move the open right fingertips back 1.5 cm, lower around its equator, and retry without sweeping.
The pinch appears above the ball. Descend the open right fingers farther toward the tabletop before closing around the isolated ball.
Avoid further downward pressure after tabletop contact. Lift, shift the right pinching zone over the ball seen below the fingertip line, and reclose at table height.
The ball is now visible within the right finger gap. Lift straight upward while closed to distinguish actual retention from table contact.
Align the isolated ball with the center of the right pinch and close at a higher height to avoid squeezing it against the table.
Make a small lateral correction to center the ball between the right finger pads, close, and test a short straight lift.
The ball is still below the effective pinching height. Lower the centered open fingers carefully to the ball's sides, then close without translating.
The ball is visible between the right finger pads. Test retention with a slow straight lift, keeping both grips closed.
The ball is now aligned with the narrow fingertip pinching zone. Reopen and close at this height, then lift gently to check whether it follows.
Top-down pinches are not retaining the ball. Withdraw and rotate the right fingers for a low horizontal approach so the pads can reach its sides without pressing into the table.
Continue changing to a horizontal right-finger approach behind the isolated front ball, preserving elbow-up continuity and leaving the held cup stationary.
Replan from the executed prefix with much smaller wrist rotations and translations; approach the ball from behind without changing elbow branch.
